items.prompt: Ruy Lopez, White to move. The knight on f6 attacks the pawn on e4, which nothing defends. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: The knight on f6 attacks e4 and no white piece defends it.
At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
After d3 the pawn on d3 defends e4.

hints: Count the attackers and defenders of e4 first.
A move can defend the pawn directly, or it can let the pawn go and get it back later.
Several moves are sound; one of them does not defend e4 at all.
items.explain: The pawn on e4 is attacked once and defended not at all. d3 and Nc3 defend it. Castling lets Black take e4, but White regains the pawn with d4 and dxe5 (the Open Ruy Lopez), so it remains one of the engine's best moves. d4 also works. All accepted moves are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best.

items.prompt: Ruy Lopez, White to move after 5...Be7. Find a sound move; one common choice defends e4 with a pawn and another with a rook.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
After Re1 the rook on e1 defends e4.
After d3 the pawn on d3 defends e4.

hints: The knight on f6 still attacks e4.
One move develops a piece; the other moves a pawn.
Both leave the knight on f3 free to move later.
items.explain: Re1 puts a rook behind the pawn; d3 puts a pawn beside it. Other moves are also sound, and all accepted moves are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best (depth 16). Masters chose Re1 more often (4,413 of 7,134 games after 5...Be7 against 2,254 for d3).

items.prompt: Ruy Lopez: White has played Re1. Black to move. Find a sound developing move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is b5 or d6, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.
The engine rates Nxe4 at least 300 centipawns lower than its best move (depth 16).
The engine rates castling at least 80 centipawns lower than its best move (depth 16).

hints: Is e4 defended now?
Count what Black gets and what Black gives for a capture on e4.
Two pawn moves are accepted, one on the queenside and one in the centre.
items.explain: Nxe4 loses a knight for a pawn: the rook on e1 takes it. At depth 16 the engine rates the capture at least 300 centipawns below its best move. b5 and d6 are within 40 centipawns of the best. Castling here is a mistake too: Bxc6 bxc6 Nxe5 wins the e5 pawn.

feedback_by_move.f6e4: The rook on e1 defends e4, so Nxe4 Rxe4 wins a knight for a pawn. At depth 16 the engine rates the capture at least 300 centipawns lower than the best move.
feedback_by_move.e8g8: Castling here loses the e5 pawn: Bxc6 bxc6 Nxe5, and the engine rates castling about a pawn below ...b5.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez: White's knight on d2 and bishop on c2 are placed and Black has played ...Re8. White to move. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
From f1 the knight attacks d2, e3, g3 and h2.

hints: The knight on d2 has no good square of its own.
Look at the squares a knight on f1 can reach next.
Several quiet moves are fine; the knight route is one plan.
items.explain: From f1 the knight can go to e3 or g3, both useful squares. a4, b3 and several other moves are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best too, so Nf1 is a plan, not the only move.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez: Black has just played ...Bf8. White to move. The knight on f1 needs a square where it defends e4 and eyes f5 and h5. Find the move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is Ng3, within 40 centipawns of it.
From g3 the knight attacks e2, e4, f1, f5, h1 and h5.

hints: Which squares does a knight on g3 attack?
The target squares are f5 and h5.
The knight on f1 can reach g3.
items.explain: A knight on g3 defends e4 and attacks f5 and h5.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez, White to move. How many white pieces defend the pawn on e4 now, and how many black pieces attack it?

claims.statement: Three white pieces defend e4: rook, bishop and knight.
Two black pieces attack e4: knight and bishop.

hints: Count the white rook, the white bishop and the white knight.
Black's bishop on b7 looks along the diagonal toward e4.
The knight on f6 also attacks e4.
items.explain: The rook on e1, the bishop on c2 and the knight on g3 defend e4. The knight on f6 and the bishop on b7 attack it. Three against two: the pawn is safe, and each piece also does something else.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pieces are now Nf6, Nd7, Bb7, Re8 and Bf8. How many black pieces defend the pawn on e5?

claims.statement: Three black pieces defend e5: pawn d6, knight d7 and rook e8.

hints: The pawn on d6 defends e5.
The knight on d7 also defends e5.
The rook on e8 sees e5 once the bishop has left e7.
items.explain: The bishop on f8 no longer blocks the e-file, so the rook on e8 defends e5 as well as the pawn on d6 and the knight on d7. That is why the retreat ...Bf8 is not a loss of time: it adds a defender.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez, Black to move after 7.Bb3. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.

hints: Castling and ...d6 are the two moves masters play most.
One of them allows an immediate d5 break by Black; the other keeps e5 guarded by a pawn first.
Developing the bishop is also fine.
items.explain: O-O, d6, Bb7 and h6 are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move at depth 16. Masters chose O-O in 2,179 games and d6 in 2,178 of 4,380 after 7.Bb3; Bb7 only 23 times. The choice is about which positions you want to play.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez, White to move. Black's bishop on b7 now eyes e4. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.

hints: Count the attackers and defenders of e4.
The bishop on b3 can add a defender to e4.
Bc2 is the most natural: it defends e4 and gives the b-pawn room.
items.explain: Bc2 adds a third defender to e4 and keeps the bishop on its diagonal. Several quiet moves are also within 40 centipawns of the engine's best (depth 16).

items.prompt: One move earlier on both sides: Black's bishop is still on f8 and White has only castled, the rook is on f1. Black plays Nxe4. Does the engine think Black is in trouble?

claims.statement: Before the capture no white piece defends e4.
After Nxe4 the engine (depth 16) rates the position between -50 and +100 centipawns for White.

hints: Is e4 defended by anything?
Compare with the position where the rook already stands on e1.
Consider what White gets for the pawn: lines and tempo.
items.explain: With the rook still on f1, nothing defends e4, but taking it leaves the engine's evaluation roughly level at depth 16: White regains the pawn with d4 and dxe5 (the Open Ruy Lopez). In the other position Black's bishop is on e7 and White's rook on e1, and the same capture loses a knight for a pawn.

items.prompt: Black has castled before playing ...d6. White to move. Find a sensible move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
After a4 the pawn on a4 attacks the pawn on b5.

hints: Is there a lever that attacks a pawn?
Is there a move that takes g4 away from the c8 bishop?
Count which of these moves keeps ...d5 from being a surprise.
items.explain: At depth 16 c3, d3, a4, h3 and several other moves are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best. c3 allows the ...d5 break (the Marshall Attack), a4 attacks b5, d3 and h3 are quieter. Masters chose a4 most often (978 games), then c3 (583).
